title: Maximum Weight and Size of Constrained Matchings in Random Bipartite Graphs
content: In this paper, we study maximum weight matchings in complete bipartite graphs with random edge states and weights, allowing for both size and length constraints. For homogenous random graphs with a common edge probability, we use stable sets in the corresponding line graphs to obtain high probability bounds for the maximum weight of a constrained matching, in terms of the inverse cumulative distribution function (cdf) of the edge weights. We also invoke martingale difference methods in conjunction with a subsequence argument to bound the fluctuations of the maximum weight around its expected value and use a weight shifting technique to demonstrate near optimal size of the maximum weight matchings with a given size constraint. Finally, we utilize iterative processes to establish bounds for the maximum weight of size constrained matchings in inhomogenous random graphs with non-uniform edge probabilities. Throughout, we illustrate our results using edge weight distributions that exhibit power law and exponential decay, respectively.
